payload.issue: The full-overwrite-per-cycle write pattern used by agent notebooks under docs/agent-memory/notebooks/*.md (read current file, append own entry, write whole file back, no lock) loses concurrent peer writers' entries under a classic lost-update race. Previously confirmed twice on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/qa.md and a qa-13.md decision-journal continuation file (see memory feedback_qa_notebook_fulloverwrite_drops_concurrent_peer_entries_20260806). This is now a 3rd occurrence, and the FIRST on a non-qa notebook: docs/agent-memory/notebooks/po.md.

evidence.instance_3: 2026-08-08T18:08Z: a peer PO triage sub-session full-overwrote docs/agent-memory/notebooks/po.md, dropping BOTH the reporting sub-session's own just-written entry AND a prior 16:00Z entry. The reporting sub-session recovered by re-appending its own section below the peer's without touching the peer's bytes -- no net data loss this time, but confirms the exposure is not qa-specific.
evidence.concurrency_confirmed: the reporting PO sub-session explicitly noted a peer PO session was running concurrently with it in the same 2026-08-08T17:37Z dev-team tick window -- i.e. two independent po triage dispatches were live at once, not just two qa-drain workers.

payload.impact: Crosses the 2+ recurring-bug escalation threshold (per feedback_recurring_bug_escalation.md) -- this is now confirmed to be a structural gap in the fleet's notebook-write mechanism generally, not an isolated qa-notebook issue, and it will keep recurring on every notebook file any time 2+ notebook-owning agent sub-sessions run concurrently (QA-drain batches, and now apparently PO triage dispatches too).
payload.requested_action: Weigh the candidate durable fix already on record (feedback_qa_notebook_fulloverwrite_drops_concurrent_peer_entries_20260806's 'How to apply' section): a commit-mutex:notebook-writes (or per-file) task_claim/task_release wrap around each notebook read-modify-write, OR a small serializing append script analogous to scripts/orch-apply.sh, applied fleet-wide across all agent-owned notebooks rather than qa-only. Route the actual mechanism decision to po (which notebooks need the lock, latency tradeoff) with implementation handed to agent-father (owns notebook-write conventions in agent flow docs) once decided.
payload.occurrence_note: 3rd occurrence overall, 1st on po.md specifically. The original 2026-08-06 signal for this pattern was deliberately NOT re-signaled on the 2nd (qa-13.md) occurrence per that memory's own note ('would re-litigate an already-surfaced decision'). Re-signaling now because occurrence 3 is new information: it demonstrates the gap is fleet-wide (any notebook, any concurrent agent-type pair), not qa-specific -- a materially different scope than what was originally surfaced.
